decision: WF-072 enforces a three-way download AND (room bulk_download, link allow_download, per-item can_download). WF-074 is already merged and owns a link record (collection wf074_link) carrying allow_download, and per-item ACL records (wf074_link_permission, wf074_dataroom_group_permission) carrying can_download. WF-072 owns the package dsr/view_only_access per the merged collision ruling. Which record ownership keeps the boundary the ruling and issue require, while leaving the three-way AND testable on its own?

state.workflow: WF-072 enforce view-only access and block bulk download

merged_reality.note: WF-074's own engine docstring already states the link switch gates the per-item flag: 'an item whose row says can_download: true is still view-only on a link whose own switch is off.'

state.ruling: orchestration/decisions/WF-072-PACKAGE-COLLISION.md (jev-20261004T145853-27760-33511) renamed WF-072's package to dsr/view_only_access and insists WF-073 (dsr/security_governance) stays untouched. WF-072's package must respect the boundary.
issue_statements: The issue's What to build names the room and link controls as WF-072's (PATCH datarooms bulkDownload, PATCH links allow_download).
The issue says: 'This issue reads and evaluates can_download; it does not own the permission set that grants it. Record that boundary rather than absorbing the other workflow.'
The AND is the feature: a test must fail when only one of the three controls permits the download.
The default is the safe one: a record written without allow_download must read as no download.
state.codebase_pattern: Each workflow namespaces its own records (wf073_*, wf074_*). A workflow reads another workflow's rows only through the store, by literal collection name, and never imports the other package (WF-074 reads WF-003's document/documentFolder rows this way).

best_approach.instructions: Which record-ownership boundary should WF-072 implement, so the three-way AND is enforced and testable in isolation while respecting the boundary the collision ruling and the issue set?

criteria.own_room_and_link_read_items: WF-072 owns its room policy (bulk_download) and its own link policy (allow_download) in namespaced wf072_* collections, and reads per-item can_download from WF-074's permission collections read-only. Matches the issue's stated API surface for room and link; honours the explicit can_download boundary; no duplicate truth for can_download; independently testable except a permission row fixture.
criteria.own_room_only_read_rest: WF-072 owns only the room policy and reads both the link allow_download and the per-item can_download from WF-074 read-only. Maximum de-duplication, but makes WF-072 depend on WF-074's private link id and shape, and gives WF-072 no link write surface the issue names.
criteria.own_all_three_duplicate: WF-072 stores all three booleans in its own records including a copy of can_download. Fully self-contained, but duplicates the per-item permission set the issue explicitly says it must not own, creating two sources of truth that can disagree.

state.change_summary: WF-072 adds a view-only access feature: a domain package dsr/view_only_access, a feature module on prefix /api/wf-072, and a frontend page under wf-072-view-only-access. Three download controls (the room's bulk_download policy, the link's allow_download policy, and the item's can_download grant read from WF-074) compose into one AND; a permitted fetch writes a wf072_view row with downloaded_at and download_type, and a refused fetch writes nothing. No shared file is edited.
